interpretation.plain_speak: Waiting for a second warning removes the early false alarms, but it also waits too long in some regimes. Under hostile pressure there is never a second warning before loss. So Wingless cannot solve the precision problem by simply demanding repeated alarms.
interpretation.north_star_question: The warning frontier is now precise enough to test the actual bounded-correction question directly: whether one frozen action on the first warning prevents more losses than it wastes, with a sham action as control.
interpretation.next_stage: test a one-shot targeted refresh on the first warning versus a same-budget sham refresh and no-action baseline, all counterfactual and policy-agnostic
